paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across media outlets

annotations.annotation: The pie chart represents the distribution of web traffic across various media sources, showing a total of 18 slices. It includes slices labeled "Breitbart" in blue at 14%, "Other" in gray at 13%, "Drudge Report" in orange at 8%, "The Daily Caller" in green at 8%, "The Huffington Post" in red at 7%, "NPR" in purple at 6%, "Vox" in brown at 6%, "The Guardian" in pink at 5%, and "BBC" in gray at 4%. There are several slices at 3%, including "RT" in light green, "Daily Kos" in light blue, "National Review" in dark blue, "Daily Mail" in pink, "Redstate" in dark red, "Fox News" in navy, "CNN" in violet, "Shareblue" in magenta, and "PoliticusUSA" in dark brown. The chart includes percentage labels inside the slices and appears to order segments from largest to smallest in an anti-clockwise direction, with none of the slices visually emphasized or exploded.
